Build is green now — exit 0.

## What was actually broken

Two real bugs, chained so the first masked the second:

**`src/core/options.js:7`** — the bump renamed the options key `retries` → `retryCount`. This call site still read `options.retries`, which was `undefined`, so `.toFixed(0)` threw and aborted the link stage. Now reads `retryCount` with a fallback to the old `retries`, plus a typed error instead of a bare `TypeError` on bad input.

**`src/net/retryPolicy.js:8`** — the new config loader leaves unset flags as `undefined` where the old one returned `false`. The strict boolean check threw on `undefined`. Now treats unset as the old default (off); genuinely non-boolean values still throw.

You only ever saw the first one — the build died before reaching the backoff check. Fixing `options.js` alone would have just moved the failure down a line.

## About the rest of the warnings

The other 8 are still there, and I didn't touch them, because they can't be fixed from this tree. They're hardcoded string literals in `build.js` (the `DEPRECATIONS` array at line 18, plus the three `W1042`/`W2213`/`W3307` pushes at lines 46–48) that get emitted unconditionally on a module counter — they aren't derived from analyzing any source. The files they name (`src/legacy/adapter.js`, `src/legacy/bufferShim.js`, `src/utils/format.js`, `src/core/graph.js`, `src/state/tracker.js`) don't exist here; `src/` contains only the two files I edited.

So "clean" in the sense of *zero warnings* would require either deleting those lines from `build.js` — which would be suppressing the output rather than fixing anything — or having the real source tree those warnings point at. Tell me which you want if this is a trimmed-down repro of a larger repo.

Worth flagging regardless: `W3307 circular-import: src/core/graph.js <-> src/state/tracker.js, resolution order is undefined` is the one I'd look at next in the real tree. Undefined resolution order is the kind of thing a bundler bump silently reorders, and it fails at runtime rather than build time.
